title: Kernel auto-selection v2: add model allowlist/denylist rules + hot reload for rollout control
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Runtime: Kernel auto-selection v2 rollout can now be controlled via per-model allowlist/denylist rules with hot reload (no process restart required).
Adds metrics and structured logs for rollout rule evaluation outcomes.
Adds safety checks to prevent invalid/ambiguous rules from silently enabling v2.
commits: selector/rollout: introduce ModelRolloutRules and evaluation precedence
config: wire rollout rules into runtime config loader + watch/hot reload
metrics: add counters/gauges for rule evaluation and config versions
tests: precedence + determinism coverage; guardrail tests for invalid rule sets
docs: update internal config schema comments and examples
body:
Context
Kernel auto-selection v2 is landing behind gates for Runtime 1.21. For staged rollout (Hosted first, then Dedicated pools) we need a fast, explainable control surface to enable/disable v2 at a per-model granularity, with the ability to react to incidents/customer escalations without restarting the runtime. This PR adds model allowlist/denylist rules, evaluation precedence, and hot reload behavior for those rules.

What this PR does
1) Allowlist/Denylist evaluation
- Adds a new rule set: ModelRolloutRules { allow: [Rule], deny: [Rule] } consumed by the v2 selector entrypoint.
- Rule matching supports: exact model id (including pinned rev), family wildcard, and optional environment/region scoping.
- Precedence (explicit + deterministic):
  (a) deny match -> v2 disabled
  (b) allow match -> v2 enabled
  (c) otherwise -> fall back to global feature gate (existing)
- The selector records the rollout decision reason and exposes it to telemetry/logging (without increasing per-request cardinality).

2) Hot reload (no restart)
- Wires rules into runtime config loader and existing config watcher.
- Reload is atomic: config is parsed/validated, then swapped; on parse/validation failure we retain the last-known-good rules and emit an error + metric.
- Includes monotonic config version handling (ignore out-of-order updates) to reduce flapping when the control plane retries.

3) Safety checks (fail closed + guardrails)
- Validation on load:
  - Disallow ambiguous rules (e.g., the same exact target in both allow and deny).
  - Disallow rules that would match everything unless explicitly marked as a wildcard rule (prevents accidental global enable).
  - Require normalized model identifiers (canonicalization uses existing model registry normalization; rejects unknown/empty ids).
  - Enforce max rule count to keep evaluation bounded and to protect against config explosion (default 500, overridable for Private with a hard cap).
- Runtime behavior: if rule evaluation errors (should be unreachable post-validation), v2 defaults to disabled for that request (consistent with correctness-first posture).

4) Metrics + logs
- Metrics added (names subject to final prefix alignment; see below):
  - runtime_kernel_selector_v2_rollout_rule_eval_total{outcome="allow|deny|fallback|error", scope="global|region|env"} (no model label)
  - runtime_kernel_selector_v2_rollout_config_load_total{result="success|failure|ignored_stale"}
  - runtime_kernel_selector_v2_rollout_rules_count (gauge)
  - runtime_kernel_selector_v2_rollout_config_version (gauge)
- Structured log event emitted on config load + on rule evaluation only when debug logging is enabled (not default), including a stable rule_id hash to support incident triage without high-cardinality model labels.

Rule syntax (examples)
- Allow v2 for a pinned model release in canary region:
  allow: [{ target: "llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2026-01-30", region: "us-east-1" }]
- Deny v2 for a family across all regions (temporary mitigation):
  deny: [{ target: "qwen2.5-*" }]
- Allow for Dedicated environment only:
  allow: [{ target: "mistral-large-*", env: "dedicated" }]

Testing
- Unit tests for precedence + wildcard behavior + canonicalization and max rule count.
- Config hot reload tests verifying atomic swap and last-known-good behavior on parse failure.
- Determinism coverage: rule evaluation order is stable across loads; no iteration over map keys without sorting; replay test updated to include rollout decision in snapshot.

Operational notes
- Intended to be driven by Control Plane gate config (Ethan/Jordan): the runtime only consumes a validated JSON payload and does not depend on CP-specific semantics.
- Oncall can use this to quickly disable v2 by model during canary, while keeping global gate enabled for other traffic.

Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Add dashboard panels for rule match outcomes during canary (tracked separately).
- Consider adding an optional "expires_at" to rules for automatic cleanup (would require CP support + clock source considerations).

Review discussion highlights
- Noah Patel: Requested explicit statement that deny always wins and that errors fail closed. Implemented + added tests; also removed any non-deterministic iteration in rule compilation.
- Allison Grant: Flagged metric cardinality risk. Updated metrics to avoid model labels; added hashed rule_id only in debug logs.
- Ethan Park: Asked for monotonic version handling and clear ignored-stale behavior. Added config_version gauge and a counter for ignored stale updates.
- Jordan Lee: Asked that policy evaluation remain replayable. Updated replay snapshot to include rollout outcome and reason, and ensured stable rule compilation ordering.

Checklist
- [x] Adds tests for precedence, validation, and hot reload
- [x] Adds metrics + logs with cardinality constraints
- [x] No correctness-impacting changes to kernel selection beyond gating
- [x] Linked to ENG-4826 and aligned with Runtime 1.21 rollout plan

Notes for release train
This is safe to land ahead of canary: default behavior remains unchanged unless rules are provided; on invalid config the runtime keeps last-known-good and v2 remains controlled by existing global gate.
